title: Monotonicity of kernel-weighted expectations
statement:
Fix a dimension $n$ and a correlation parameter $\rho$ with $0 \le \rho \le 1$, and let $K_\rho(x,y) = \prod_{i} \tfrac{1 + \rho\,\chi(x_i)\,\chi(y_i)}{2}$ denote the noise kernel on the Boolean hypercube $\{0,1\}^n$, where $\chi(\cdot)$ is the $\pm 1$ encoding of a bit. If $h, h' : \{0,1\}^n \times \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ satisfy $h(x,y) \le h'(x,y)$ for all $x$ and $y$, then the kernel-weighted average of $h$ is at most that of $h'$:
\[
  \frac{1}{2^n}\sum_{x}\sum_{y} K_\rho(x,y)\, h(x,y)
  \;\le\;
  \frac{1}{2^n}\sum_{x}\sum_{y} K_\rho(x,y)\, h'(x,y).
\]
hypotheses_covered: h(x,y) ≤ h'(x,y) for all x, y
